Class TypeHierarchyFuzz

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.inject.test.hierarchy.TypeHierarchyFuzz
public final class TypeHierarchyFuzz extends Object
Generates random generic hierarchies in Java, Kotlin or Python source, and checks the TypeHierarchy the compiler recorded for each against the hierarchy java.lang.reflect reads from the compiled class: the closure of the declaration, of a raw parameterization and of a concrete one.

The grammar covers type variables with simple, recursive and intersection bounds, nested type arguments, arrays and arrays of arrays, of a primitive among them, the three kinds of wildcard, raw and parameterized super classes, and diamonds. A language that lacks a feature (Kotlin has no raw types, Python has neither wildcards nor arrays) leaves it out. A type naming the class being declared is never produced: the javac element resolves the arguments of such a self reference to Object.

    • checkPython

      public static List<String> checkPython(TypeHierarchyFuzz.Generated g, Class<?> type, TypeHierarchy hierarchy)
      Compares the record of a generated Python class with the hierarchy the generator declared. The Java stub of a Python class carries neither its Python bases nor its type variables in its reflective signature, so the reference is the model itself: the helper classes of the prelude with their declared super types, the Java interfaces of the JDK through reflection.
      Parameters:
      g - The generated class
      type - The compiled class
      hierarchy - Its record
      Returns:
      The mismatches, empty when the record agrees with the declaration
